summary: storage-init.test.ts passes code review. The file is well-structured, properly isolated (each test owns its temp dir via makeTempDir), and follows every project convention established in json-storage.test.ts. All five acceptance criteria are met. The three unique tests — partial initialization scenario, doesNotThrow idempotency, and byte-for-byte file-stability — add meaningful coverage beyond what existed in json-storage.test.ts. One medium-priority maintenance observation recorded (test duplication); no blocking issues found; no Fix-Forward edits applied.

comments.note: 7 of the 10 tests in storage-init.test.ts duplicate initializeStorage tests already present in json-storage.test.ts (directory creation ×3, seed-file JSON structure ×2, idempotency ×2). When initializeStorage changes, both files will need updating. The 3 unique tests (partial-init scenario, doesNotThrow idempotency, byte-for-byte stability) justify the dedicated file, but the 7 duplicates increase maintenance surface. Consider consolidating the json-storage.test.ts initializeStorage block into storage-init.test.ts and removing the duplicates from json-storage.test.ts in a future cleanup WP.

makeConfig() in storage-init.test.ts carries an explicit ': AppConfig' return type annotation — this is strictly better than the implicit return type on makeTestConfig() in json-storage.test.ts. The annotation contracts the helper to the production type, so any field additions/removals in AppConfig will cause a compile-time error in the test helper. No action needed here; this is a pattern worth replicating in the companion file.
